ingredients: 1.5 kg chicken or turkey pieces, plus 2 litres water and 1/2 onion for broth
6 chilhuacle negro chiles, stemmed and seeded (substitute extra mulato chiles)
6 mulato chiles and 4 pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
50 g each sesame seeds, almonds and peanuts
30 g raisins and 1 ripe plantain, sliced and fried
1 slice stale bread and 1 stale tortilla, toasted until blackened
1 tsp each dried oregano, thyme, black pepper; 4 cloves; 5 cm canela (Ceylon cinnamon)
90 g Oaxacan chocolate tablet and 2 hoja santa leaves (avellano/yerba santa)
steps: Simmer the poultry with onion, salt and water for 45 minutes until tender, then reserve the meat and broth.
Toast the chiles on a dry comal until very dark but not ashen, reserve the seeds and char them black, then soak the chiles in hot broth for 20 minutes.
Toast the nuts, seeds and spices separately over low heat until fragrant, and fry the raisins, plantain, bread and tortilla in a little lard.
Blend the chiles, charred seeds, roasted vegetables, toasted ingredients and fried ingredients with broth in batches to a very smooth paste, straining if needed.

Fry the paste in hot lard in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring constantly for 20 minutes, then add chocolate, hoja santa and 1 litre broth and simmer gently for 60 minutes until glossy and coating the spoon.
Add the meat for the last 15 minutes, season with salt and a pinch of sugar, and serve with white rice and hot corn tortillas.

150 g ibes (Yucatecan white lima beans), cooked, or butter beans
1 small cabbage wedge, shredded, and tomato salsa to serve
steps: Mash the cooked ibes with the ground pumpkin seeds, spring onions and a pinch of salt.
Knead the masa with salt; take 12 balls, flatten into thick discs, add a spoon of filling and close into a torpedo shape (polcan means "snake head" in Maya).
Fry in 3 cm hot oil (180°C) for 4–5 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with shredded cabbage and tomato-habanero salsa.

ingredients: 1 turkey breast and 2 thighs (about 2 kg) or 2 kg chicken pieces
100 g recado negro (chilmole, burnt chile paste)
For the but (stuffing): 500 g ground pork, 1 egg, 2 tomatoes, 1/2 onion, 30 g recado negro
steps: Dissolve 100 g recado negro in some water and rub it over the turkey; put in a large pot with the charred onion, garlic, tomatoes, oregano, salt and the water.
Bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 1.5–2 hours until the turkey is very tender.

Mix the ground pork with the raw egg, chopped tomato, onion and remaining recado negro, shape around the hard-boiled yolks into a log, wrap in cloth or foil, and poach in the broth for 40 minutes until cooked through (71°C).
Whisk the masa harina with some broth and stir into the pot; simmer 10 minutes until the black broth thickens slightly.
Serve the turkey with slices of the stuffing (but) in the black broth, with tortillas; leftovers make excellent tortas.

ingredients: 2 kg turkey pieces (or a whole small turkey)
1 tbsp recado de especia (black pepper, clove, cinnamon, oregano paste)
For the stuffing: 500 g ground pork, 50 g raisins, 30 g capers, 50 g green olives chopped, 2 tomatoes chopped, 2 eggs
steps: Rub the turkey with recado de especia and salt, then simmer with the roasted garlic, chile and water for 1.5–2 hours until tender.

Sauté the ground pork with tomato, raisins, capers and olives for 10 minutes, cool slightly, mix in the raw eggs and shape into a log around the hard-boiled eggs; wrap and poach in the broth 40 minutes until cooked through.
Thicken the broth with the flour whisked into cold broth, simmering 10 minutes into a pale, creamy kol (white sauce).
Serve the turkey and slices of stuffing in the white sauce, with tortillas and pickled habanero.

ingredients: 1 Edam cheese ball (about 1.5 kg), top cut off and hollowed (keep shell 1.5 cm thick)
50 g raisins, 30 g capers, 50 g olives chopped
1 tsp recado de especia (or 1/2 tsp each black pepper and allspice)
For kol (white sauce): 500 ml chicken broth, 2 tbsp flour, pinch saffron or achiote
For tomato sauce: 4 tomatoes, 1/2 onion, 1 xcatic chile
steps: Sauté the onion and tomatoes in a little oil, add the pork and recado de especia and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes until browned and cooked; stir in raisins, capers, olives and egg.
Pack the filling into the hollowed Edam shell, replace the lid, wrap in cheesecloth and steam for 15–20 minutes until the cheese softens.
Make the kol by whisking the flour into the broth with saffron and simmering until thickened; make the tomato sauce by blending and simmering tomatoes with onion and chile for 10 minutes.
Unwrap the cheese, cut into wedges, and serve covered with the white sauce and tomato sauce.

ingredients: 1 kg pork (shoulder, ribs and a piece of skin), in chunks
To serve: chiltomate (roasted tomato-habanero salsa), chopped radish, cilantro, onion, lime, white rice
steps: Drain the beans and simmer with the water, onion and epazote for 1 hour.
Add the pork and salt and simmer for another 1.5 hours until the pork is very tender and the beans are creamy.
Make chiltomate by charring 4 tomatoes and 1 habanero, then blending with salt.
Serve the beans and pork in bowls with rice, chiltomate, radish, cilantro, onion and lime; this is the classic Monday lunch in Yucatán.

ingredients: 1 kg masa (or 600 g masa harina + 750 ml chicken broth)
1 kg chicken pieces, cooked and shredded (reserve 1 litre broth)
500 g pork shoulder, cooked and shredded
4 tbsp masa harina, for the kol
steps: Whisk the masa with the lard, salt and a little broth until light and spreadable.
Make the kol by whisking 4 tbsp masa harina and 20 g recado rojo into 1 litre broth and simmering until thick; stir in the meats with tomato, onion and epazote, plus remaining recado.
Line a deep roasting pan with banana leaves, press in two-thirds of the masa up the sides, fill with the meat and kol, then cover with the remaining masa and seal; fold leaves over.
Bake at 180°C for 1.5–2 hours (or bury in a pib earth oven, traditionally for Hanal Pixán in early November) until the crust is firm and golden.
Rest 20 minutes, cut into squares and serve with habanero salsa.

ingredients: banana leaves, cut into 25 cm squares and softened
steps: Dissolve the masa harina in 1.2 litres broth, strain through a sieve (colado), then cook with the lard and salt over medium heat, stirring constantly for 20 minutes until it is a thick, glossy paste; cool to set.
Make kol by whisking a little masa into the remaining broth with recado rojo and simmering until thick; mix in the chicken.
Spread a square of masa on each banana leaf, add chicken, a slice of tomato and onion and an epazote leaf, then fold into parcels.
Steam for 1 hour until the masa is set and wobbly-soft; serve hot.

ingredients: 500 g pork or chicken, cooked and shredded
3 tbsp masa harina whisked into 400 ml broth for kol
banana leaves, cut into 25 cm squares and softened
steps: Beat the masa harina with broth, lard and salt into a soft, spreadable dough.
Simmer the kol (broth, masa and recado rojo) until thick, then mix in the shredded meat.
Spread a very thin layer of masa (2–3 mm) on each banana leaf, add a spoon of filling and a tomato slice, and fold into flat rectangles.
Steam for 1 hour until the masa is cooked and pulls away from the leaf; serve with habanero salsa.

ingredients: 800 g masa harina dough (500 g masa harina + 650 ml water)
15 chaya leaves, blanched and chopped (or spinach)

30 g extra ground pumpkin seeds, for garnish

Spread the masa about 1 cm thick into a large rectangle on a banana leaf, sprinkle with ground pumpkin seeds and chopped egg, and roll up into a thick log (the "queen's arm").
Wrap tightly in banana leaves and steam for 1.5 hours until firm.
Slice and serve topped with tomato-habanero sauce and a sprinkle of pumpkin seeds.

ingredients: 500 g cazón (dogfish/small shark), or firm white fish such as cod
500 ml tomato sauce (blended tomatoes, onion, habanero, simmered)
steps: Poach the fish in salted water with epazote for 10 minutes until it flakes, then drain, cool and shred, discarding bones and skin.

Warm the tortillas; spread one with beans, top with fish, cover with a second bean-spread tortilla, and stack three layers high.
Place each stack on a plate, cover generously with hot tomato sauce and serve, as in Campeche.

steps: Blend the recado rojo with bitter orange juice, garlic and salt into a paste.
Rub the paste over the flesh side of the fish and marinate 1–2 hours in the fridge.
Lay the fish skin-side down on banana leaves, top with tomato, onion and pepper, and fold the leaves over.
Grill over medium charcoal for 25–30 minutes (or bake at 200°C) until the flesh is opaque and flakes at the thickest part.
Serve with rice, tortillas, pickled onion and habanero salsa.

ingredients: 1 turkey or 2 kg chicken pieces, plus 2.5 litres water, 1/2 onion and 2 garlic cloves for broth
6 mulato, 6 ancho and 4 pasilla chiles, seeded (seeds reserved)
3 tomatoes and 4 tomatillos, roasted, plus 1/2 onion and 6 garlic cloves
60 g sesame seeds, 50 g almonds, 30 g peanuts and 30 g pepitas
50 g raisins, 1 ripe plantain and 1 stale tortilla plus 1 slice bread, fried
1/2 tsp each anise, black pepper, coriander seed; 5 cloves; 5 cm canela
steps: Simmer the poultry with onion, garlic and salt for 50–60 minutes until tender and reserve meat and broth.
Fry the chiles briefly in lard until they blister, then soak in hot broth for 20 minutes.
Toast the sesame (keep 2 tbsp for garnish), nuts, pepitas, spices and chile seeds, and fry the raisins, plantain, tortilla and bread.

600 g mixed ground pork and beef

1 apple, 1 pear and 1 peach, diced, plus 1 plantain, diced

200 g fresh walnuts (nuez de Castilla), peeled
100 g fresh goat cheese and 250 ml milk
1 pomegranate, seeds only, and a few parsley leaves

Soak the peeled walnuts in milk for 30 minutes, then blend with goat cheese, sugar, sherry and a pinch of salt to a smooth, pourable white sauce (nogada).
Stuff each chile generously with the picadillo, served at room temperature as tradition calls for (plain, or battered and fried capeado-style if preferred).
Cover with nogada and decorate with pomegranate seeds and parsley to show the green, white and red of the flag.

steps: Mix flour, sugar, yolks, lard and milk into a smooth dough, roll 5 mm thick and cut into 7 cm rounds.
Bake at 180 C for 12–15 minutes until just golden at the edges, then cool.
Boil sugar and water to a thick syrup (112 C), stir in the ground pepitas and beat until it turns opaque and creamy.
Spread a thick mound of pepita cream on each cookie and let it set for 1 hour.

ingredients: 2 tbsp lard and 1 tsp baking powder
steps: Knead flour, eggs, lard, baking powder, salt and water to a firm dough, rest 15 minutes, then roll thin and cut into 2 cm squares.
Fry the squares at 175 C for 2–3 minutes until puffed and golden, and drain.
Melt the piloncillo with water and canela over medium heat and boil 8 minutes to a thick syrup.
Toss the fried pieces in the syrup and press into small clusters on oiled paper, then let them harden before serving.

ingredients: 5 cm canela and 1 vanilla pod, split
steps: Bring the milk, sugar, canela, vanilla and baking soda to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes and cool slightly.
Beat the yolks until pale, then slowly whisk in a ladle of hot milk to temper them.
Return everything to the pot with the almonds and cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it reaches 75 C and coats a spoon; do not boil.
Strain, cool completely, stir in the rum if using, bottle and chill, and serve cold in small glasses dusted with cinnamon.

ingredients: 1.2 kg pork shoulder, sliced 5 mm thick
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 1/2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp salt
1/2 fresh pineapple, peeled and sliced into rings
1 white onion and 1 bunch cilantro, finely chopped, plus lime wedges and salsa verde to serve
steps: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 seconds per side, then soak in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the drained chiles with achiote, pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin and salt into a smooth adobo; coat the pork slices thoroughly and marinate covered in the fridge overnight.

Stack the pork slices tightly on a skewer set in a halved onion (a home "trompo") and roast at 220°C for 35–40 minutes until edges char and the centre reaches 70°C; alternatively sear slices in a very hot comal 3 minutes per side.
Grill the pineapple rings over high heat for 3–4 minutes per side until caramelised, then chop.
Shave the pork thinly, crisp it briefly on the hot comal, and pile onto doubled warm tortillas with pineapple, onion, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and salsa verde.

ingredients: 200 g chicharrón prensado or shredded cooked pork in adobo
Salsa verde cruda and pickled jalapeños to serve
steps: Fry the chorizo for 6–8 minutes over medium heat until cooked through, then mix it into the mashed potato.
Blend the guajillos with garlic, salt, a little soaking water and 3 tbsp lard into a thin red sauce; warm the remaining lard with the sliced onion until soft.
Dip each tortilla briefly in the red sauce, fill with potato-chorizo, beans or chicharrón, and fold in half.
Line a basket or deep pot with a cloth and plastic, layer the tacos tightly, drizzling hot onion lard between each layer, then wrap and steam-sweat them for 40 minutes until soft and glossy.
Serve warm straight from the basket with salsa verde cruda and pickled jalapeños.

ingredients: 1.2 kg beef suadero (rose meat / brisket flap), cut into strips
Chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa roja to serve
steps: Put the beef, onion, garlic, bay leaves and salt in a pot, cover with water and simmer gently for 1.5 hours until tender, then drain well.
Melt the lard in a wide pan or a "choricera" comal over medium heat and confit the beef in it for 40–60 minutes until the edges turn golden and crisp.
Lift the meat out, chop it finely on a board, and return it briefly to the edge of the fat to keep hot.
Dip the tortillas in the hot fat for a few seconds, double them, and fill with suadero.
Top with onion and cilantro and serve with lime and salsa roja.

ingredients: 1 kg beef small intestine (tripa), thoroughly cleaned
Chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa roja to serve
steps: Rinse the tripa inside and out under running water several times until the water runs clear.
Simmer it with onion, garlic, bay leaves and salt for about 1.5 hours until tender, then drain and pat very dry.
Fry the tripa in hot lard over medium-high heat for 15–20 minutes, turning, until crisp and deeply golden (or leave softer "suave" if preferred).
Chop into small pieces, crisp once more on the comal, and fill warm doubled tortillas.
Serve with onion, cilantro, lime and a fiery salsa roja.

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef cheeks (cachete), plus tongue (lengua) if available
Chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa verde to serve
steps: Put the cheeks and tongue in a large pot with onion, garlic, bay, oregano and salt, cover with water and simmer for 3–4 hours until meltingly tender.
Peel the outer skin from the tongue while warm and discard it.
Chop the meats separately, then keep them moist in a steamer basket over the hot broth for 10 minutes so they stay juicy.
Steam the tortillas in the same steamer for 1 minute until soft.
Fill doubled tortillas with the cut of choice and serve with onion, cilantro, lime and salsa verde.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 300 g Mexican pork chorizo, casing removed
150 g chicharrón (fried pork rind), broken into pieces
Chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa roja to serve
steps: Fry the chorizo in a hot pan for 6–8 minutes until fully cooked and crumbly, then set aside.
Sear the steak in hot lard over high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until browned and cooked through, then chop finely and season with salt.
Toss steak and chorizo together on the comal for 1 minute, then add the chicharrón just before serving so it stays crunchy.
Fill warm doubled tortillas with the mixed meats.
Top with onion and cilantro and serve with lime and salsa roja.

steps: Boil the tomatillos, tomatoes and serranos for 8 minutes until soft, then blend with garlic and salt into a green-red salsa.
Brown the pork in the lard over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, add the onion and cook until soft.
Pour in the salsa, cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce coats it.
Spread a spoonful of red rice on doubled warm tortillas and top with the guisado (and a slice of egg if using).
Serve straight away, as the taquerías de guisado do, with extra salsa on the side.

ingredients: 500 g cooked al pastor pork, chopped
250 g Oaxaca cheese (quesillo), shredded; mozzarella as a substitute
Chopped onion, cilantro and salsa verde to serve
steps: Heat a comal or large pan over medium heat and lightly oil it.
Lay a flour tortilla down, scatter with cheese, then al pastor meat and a little pineapple, and cover with a second tortilla.
Cook for 2–3 minutes per side until the tortilla is golden and the cheese fully melted.
Cut into quarters and serve with onion, cilantro and salsa verde.

ingredients: 500 g masa harina (or fresh nixtamal masa), mixed with 650 ml warm water and 1 tsp salt
200 g mushrooms, sliced, sautéed with epazote and garlic
200 g squash blossoms (flor de calabaza), cleaned
100 ml crema and 60 g crumbled queso fresco
steps: Knead the masa until soft and smooth like play-dough, then rest covered for 10 minutes.
Sauté the squash blossoms with onion in the oil for 3 minutes until wilted.
Press a ball of masa into a 15 cm oval tortilla, fill one half with quesillo plus mushrooms or squash blossoms, and fold to seal the edges.
Cook on a hot comal over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until speckled and cooked through (or deep-fry until golden for the street version).
Open slightly and spoon in crema, queso fresco and salsa verde before serving.

ingredients: 500 g blue corn masa (or masa harina with 650 ml warm water)
300 g refried pinto beans or requesón
steps: Knead the masa with salt until smooth and divide into 8 balls.
Flatten each ball, place a spoonful of beans in the centre, fold the masa over it and press into a thick oval about 1 cm deep.
Cook on a dry comal over medium heat for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through with toasted spots.
Top each tlacoyo with salsa verde, nopales, onion, cilantro and queso fresco and serve hot.

ingredients: 500 g masa harina with 650 ml warm water and 1 tsp salt
150 ml salsa verde and 150 ml salsa roja
steps: Knead the masa smooth, divide into 4 balls, stuff each with beans and press into a long sandal-shaped oval about 30 cm long.
Cook on a hot comal for 4 minutes per side until set, then drizzle with a little lard and crisp the edges.
Season and sear the steak in hot lard for 2 minutes per side until cooked through, then chop.
Spread half of each huarache with salsa verde and half with salsa roja, top with steak, crema, queso fresco, onion and cilantro, and serve hot.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 6 guajillo chiles, seeded, toasted and soaked
100 ml crema and 80 g queso fresco, crumbled
steps: Blend the guajillos with garlic, salt and 150 ml soaking water into a smooth red sauce.
Fry the chorizo for 6–8 minutes until cooked, then add the potatoes and cook for 5 minutes until lightly crisp.
Split the rolls, dip the outsides fully in the guajillo sauce, and fry in hot lard for 1–2 minutes per side until the bread is red and slightly crisp.
Fill with chorizo-potato, lettuce, crema, queso fresco and salsa verde, and eat immediately.

ingredients: 4 tamales verdes or rojos (pork or chicken), freshly steamed
4 cups atole or champurrado to serve
steps: Steam the tamales for 10–15 minutes until hot through, then unwrap them.
Split the rolls and toast the cut sides in butter on a comal over medium heat for 1–2 minutes.
Tuck a whole tamal inside each roll and spoon over a little salsa verde.
Serve at breakfast with a cup of hot atole or champurrado, as sold at Mexico City street stands.

ingredients: 4 ears white corn (elote), kernels cut off (about 600 g)
1 lime, plus chile piquín powder or Tajín
steps: Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion and serrano for 3 minutes.
Add the corn kernels, epazote, salt and 500 ml water; simmer for 20 minutes until the corn is tender and the broth fragrant.
Spoon the corn with a little broth into cups.
Top each with mayonnaise, cotija, a squeeze of lime and a dusting of chile piquín, and serve hot.

ingredients: 4 thin beef or pork cutlets (about 120 g each), pounded thin
4 tbsp mayonnaise and pickled jalapeños (chiles en vinagre)
steps: Season the cutlets with salt, dip in beaten egg and press into breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through; drain on paper.
Split and toast the teleras on the comal, then spread the bottom with beans and the top with mayonnaise.
Layer milanesa, avocado, tomato, onion and jalapeños, close and press lightly before serving.

ingredients: 2 thin beef milanesas, breaded and fried
100 g Oaxaca cheese and 2 slices American cheese
100 g refried beans, 1 avocado, sliced tomato and onion
steps: Fry the sausages and ham on a hot griddle for 2–3 minutes until browned, and fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Melt the Oaxaca and American cheese on the griddle over the ham.
Toast the split teleras, spread the bottoms with beans and the tops with mayonnaise.
Pile in milanesa, ham with cheese, sausages, chorizo, egg, avocado, tomato, onion and jalapeños, press together and halve to serve.

ingredients: 500 g masa harina with 650 ml warm water and 1 tsp salt
steps: Blend the guajillos, tomatillos and garlic, then simmer with the chicharrón prensado for 10 minutes until thick.
Knead half the chicharrón mixture into the masa, form 8 balls and press into thick 10 cm discs.
Cook on a comal over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side until puffed, then fry briefly in lard until crisp outside.
Slit each gordita open like a pocket, fill with the remaining chicharrón, onion, cilantro and queso fresco, and serve hot.

ingredients: 200 g Oaxaca or Chihuahua cheese, shredded
steps: Heat a comal or large pan over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Lay down a tortilla, cover with cheese and ham, add more cheese, and top with another tortilla.
Cook for 2–3 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with guacamole and salsa roja.

ingredients: 4 tbsp Valentina or Mexican hot sauce
steps: Heat the oil to 190°C in a deep pot.
Drop in the dried pinwheels a few at a time; they puff within 5–10 seconds — turn them and lift out as soon as fully puffed and pale gold.
Drain on paper and sprinkle with salt and chile powder while hot.
Serve in bags or bowls with lime juice and hot sauce poured over, as street vendors do.

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef tripe (pancita / mondongo), cleaned and cut into pieces
6 guajillo chiles and 2 ancho chiles, seeded and soaked
Chopped onion, lime wedges, chile de árbol flakes and warm tortillas to serve
steps: Rinse the tripe well, then boil it for 5 minutes, drain and rinse again to clean it.
Return to a large pot with the beef foot, onion, 4 garlic cloves, bay leaves, salt and 4 litres water; simmer for 2.5 hours until tender.
Blend the soaked chiles with the remaining garlic and a little broth, strain into the pot, and simmer another 30 minutes.
Serve very hot with oregano rubbed between the palms, chopped onion, lime, chile flakes and tortillas.

ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces on the bone
2 chipotles in adobo, plus 1 tbsp adobo
1 avocado, 100 g queso fresco or Oaxaca cheese, lime wedges to serve
steps: Simmer the chicken with half onion, garlic and salt for 35 minutes until cooked through; remove, shred and strain the broth.
Blend the tomatoes with chipotles and adobo; fry the chopped onion in a little oil, add the purée and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the broth, carrots and chickpeas and simmer for 10 minutes, then the zucchini, green beans and epazote for 5 minutes more.
Return the chicken, check salt, and serve with cubes of avocado and cheese and lime wedges.

ingredients: 1 garlic clove and a handful of cilantro
250 ml crema (Mexican cream; sour cream thinned with milk as substitute)
200 g Manchego or Chihuahua cheese, grated
steps: Boil the tomatillos and serranos for 8 minutes, then blend with onion, garlic, cilantro, salt and the crema into a smooth green sauce.
Fry the sauce in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Soften the tortillas in the remaining hot oil for a few seconds each, fill with chicken, roll and arrange in a baking dish.
Pour over the sauce, cover with cheese and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until the cheese melts and browns in spots; serve hot.

ingredients: 4 thin beef tenderloin or skirt steaks (about 200 g each)
1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp black pepper
4 poblano chiles, roasted, peeled and cut in strips (rajas)
4 enchiladas verdes or rojas, 200 g refried beans, guacamole and Mexican rice to serve
steps: Marinate the steaks with lime juice, garlic, salt and pepper in the fridge overnight (or at least 2 hours).
Sauté the poblano rajas with onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Grill the panela slices in a dry pan for 1 minute per side until golden.
Sear the steaks over very high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until well browned and cooked to your liking.
Plate each steak with rajas, an enchilada, beans, rice, guacamole and grilled panela, in the classic Tampico-style platter.

ingredients: 500 g tomatoes and 2 chipotles in adobo
3 poblano chiles, roasted, peeled and cut in strips
250 g Manchego or Chihuahua cheese, grated
steps: Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, onion, garlic and salt, then fry in 1 tbsp oil for 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Fry the tortillas briefly in hot oil for 5 seconds each to soften and seal them.
Layer in a greased dish: tortillas, sauce, chicken, poblano rajas, corn, crema and cheese; repeat 3 times, finishing with sauce, crema and cheese.
Bake covered at 180°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered 10 minutes until bubbling and golden; rest 5 minutes before cutting.

ingredients: 1 kg romeritos (seepweed), washed; baby spinach or samphire as substitute
steps: Boil the romeritos for 5 minutes, drain and squeeze dry; boil the potatoes and nopales separately until tender.
Dissolve the mole paste in hot stock over medium heat, stirring, and simmer 10 minutes until smooth and thick.
Grind the dried shrimp, mix with eggs and breadcrumbs, form small patties and fry in hot lard for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Add romeritos, potatoes, nopales and shrimp patties to the mole, simmer 10 minutes, and serve hot for Christmas Eve or Lent with rice and tortillas.

ingredients: 1 tbsp sugar plus 100 g sugar mixed with 1 tsp ground cinnamon for coating
150 g Mexican chocolate tablets (Abuelita or Ibarra), chopped
steps: Bring water, 1 tbsp sugar, salt and butter to a boil, add the flour all at once and stir vigorously for 1 minute into a smooth dough; cool 10 minutes.
Pipe the dough through a star nozzle into oil heated to 180°C in 15 cm lengths and fry for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and roll the hot churros in cinnamon sugar.
Heat the milk with the chocolate, whisking (or using a wooden molinillo) until dissolved and frothy, about 5 minutes.
Serve the churros hot with cups of chocolate for dunking, as at El Moro in the Centro Histórico.

ingredients: 250 g piloncillo or dark brown sugar
60 g peanuts, pepitas or raisins to decorate
steps: Melt the piloncillo with water, honey and lime juice over medium heat, stirring, then boil without stirring for 8–10 minutes until it reaches the soft-ball stage (115°C).
Pour the hot syrup over the amaranth and mix quickly until evenly coated.
Press firmly into a greased tray or round moulds about 2 cm thick and decorate with peanuts, pepitas or raisins.
Cool for 30 minutes until set, then cut into bars or rounds and store airtight.

ingredients: 2 kg goat (chivo) on the bone, cut in large pieces (substitute lamb shoulder)
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 1/2 tsp cumin, 4 cloves, 1 small cinnamon stick (canela)
steps: Toast the dried chiles in a dry comal over medium heat for 20-30 seconds a side until fragrant, then soak them in hot water for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the chiles with onion, garlic, vinegar, oregano, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, salt and a little soaking water into a thick adobo; rub it all over the goat and marinate overnight in the fridge.

Set the meat on a rack in a deep roasting pan with 750 ml water and the bay leaves below, seal tightly with foil (traditionally a clay pot sealed with masa), and bake at 160 C for 3.5-4 hours until the meat falls off the bone.
Roast the tomatoes until blistered, blend them, and simmer with the pan juices for 15 minutes to make the consommé, skimming excess fat and seasoning with salt.
Serve the meat in bowls with hot consommé ladled over, with chopped onion, cilantro, lime, salsa de chile de árbol and warm corn tortillas.

ingredients: 4 birote salado rolls (substitute crusty sourdough baguette rolls)
1 tsp dried oregano, pinch of cumin, 1 tsp salt
25 chiles de árbol, stemmed (for the hot salsa)
1 white onion, thinly sliced and soaked in lime juice with salt
steps: Simmer the tomatoes, onion and garlic in 500 ml water for 15 minutes, blend with oregano, cumin and salt, strain and simmer 10 minutes more to make the mild tomato bath.
For the picante, toast the chiles de árbol 20 seconds, soak in hot water 10 minutes, then blend with vinegar, a garlic clove, salt and 250 ml water and strain.
Split the rolls, spread with refried beans and fill generously with carnitas.
Set each torta in a deep plate, pour the warm tomato salsa over to drown (ahogar) it and add the chile de árbol salsa to taste.
Top with lime-pickled onions and eat at once with a spoon and plenty of napkins.

ingredients: 1.2 kg pork shoulder and 500 g pork neck bones (or half pig's head, traditional)
2 x 820 g cans white hominy (maíz pozolero), drained and rinsed
1 head garlic, halved, plus 3 cloves for the sauce
6 guajillo chiles and 3 ancho chiles, seeded
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, plus more to serve
1/2 small green cabbage, finely shredded, 8 radishes, sliced
steps: Cover the pork and bones with 4 litres water, add the halved onion, garlic head and salt, bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Toast the chiles 30 seconds per side, soak 15 minutes in hot water, then blend with 3 garlic cloves, oregano and 250 ml soaking liquid and strain.
Add the hominy and the red chile purée to the pot and simmer 40 minutes more until the kernels bloom open and the broth is brick red.
Remove the bones, shred the meat back into the pot and adjust the salt.
Serve in deep bowls with cabbage, radish, onion, oregano, ground chile piquín, lime and tostadas on the side.

ingredients: 700 g beef sirloin or flank, sliced paper-thin and cut into small pieces
2 cups cooked pinto beans (frijoles de la olla) with some broth
steps: Fry the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp; lift it out and keep the fat.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos for 8 minutes until olive green, then blend with onion, garlic, half the cilantro and a cup of broth.
Sear the beef in the bacon fat over high heat in batches, about 2 minutes, season with salt and pepper, then pour in the tomatillo sauce and the rest of the broth.
Simmer 20 minutes until the beef is cooked through and tender and the broth is savoury.
Ladle into bowls with a spoonful of beans and their broth, and top with the crisp bacon, chopped onion, cilantro, radishes and lime, with tortillas alongside.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 4 cups cooked bayo or peruano beans, with 1 cup of their broth
150 g Mexican pork chorizo, casing removed
4 pickled jalapeños, chopped, plus 2 tbsp of their brine
100 g queso Chihuahua or Monterey Jack, grated
steps: Melt the lard in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the bacon and chorizo for 8 minutes until browned and the chorizo fat runs red.
Add the beans with a little broth and mash them in the pan with a bean masher, cooking 8-10 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in the jalapeños, brine and olives, adjust the salt, and loosen with broth if needed.
Top with the grated cheese, cover for 2 minutes until it melts, and serve hot with tortilla chips (totopos) or alongside grilled meats.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 1 whole chicken (1.5 kg), cut in pieces
4 guajillo chiles and 2 ancho chiles, seeded
1 cup corn masa harina (or 250 g fresh masa)
steps: Simmer the chicken with half the onion, 2 garlic cloves, bay leaf and salt in 2.5 litres water for 40 minutes until cooked through; reserve the broth and shred the meat.
Toast and soak the chiles, then blend with tomatoes, remaining onion and garlic, cumin and cloves, and strain.
Fry the sauce in the lard in a heavy pot for 5 minutes over medium heat until it darkens.
Whisk the masa harina into 1.5 litres of the warm broth until smooth, then pour it into the sauce, stirring constantly over low heat for 15-20 minutes until thick like a loose polenta.
Fold in the shredded chicken, season and serve hot in bowls with tostadas and pickled chiles, as is done in southern Jalisco and Colima.

ingredients: 1 whole snapper or robalo (1.5-2 kg), butterflied through the back, scaled and gutted
2 tbsp salsa negra or Worcestershire sauce
steps: Blend the soaked chiles with garlic, mayonnaise, salsa negra, soy, lime juice and salt into a smooth red paste.
Season the opened fish with salt and lime and brush the flesh side generously with the paste; leave 20 minutes.
Clamp the fish in an oiled fish-grilling basket (zaranda) and grill over medium-hot mangrove wood or charcoal, skin side down first for 12-15 minutes.
Flip, baste again and grill the flesh side 8-10 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily at the thickest part.
Serve on the board with warm tortillas, sliced cucumber, onion, avocado and salsa so diners build tacos, Nayarit style.

ingredients: 600 g very fresh sushi-grade firm white fish (sierra or mahi-mahi), or raw shrimp
steps: Use only sashimi/sushi-grade fish kept ice-cold; mince it finely with a sharp knife or pulse it in a cold food processor (the Nayarit style is finely ground).
Cover the fish with lime juice and salt in a glass bowl and refrigerate 20-25 minutes, stirring once, until it turns opaque white.
Squeeze out some excess juice, then fold in the carrot, cucumber, onion, serrano and cilantro and season with salsa negra.
Serve chilled piled on crisp tostadas with sliced avocado and hot sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 cups masa harina mixed with 1.5 cups warm water and 1/2 tsp salt
2 cups finely shredded cabbage, 6 radishes sliced
steps: Shape the masa into 30 small balls and press into 7 cm discs; cook on a hot comal 1 minute per side, then pinch the edges to form a little rim.
Fry the ground beef in a tablespoon of oil with the carrot and potato for 10-12 minutes until browned and cooked through; season with salt.
Blend the tomatoes with onion, garlic and oregano and simmer 10 minutes into a thin, mild salsa.
Fry the sopitos briefly in hot oil, about 30 seconds a side, until golden at the edges, and drain.
Top each with beef, a spoon of the warm tomato broth, cabbage, radish and cotija, and serve with hot sauce.
recipe.source: AI-written (Claude) — not yet reviewed by a cook

ingredients: 2 x 820 g cans white hominy, drained and rinsed
4 guajillo chiles and 2 ancho chiles, seeded
1 tsp dried Mexican oregano, 1/2 tsp cumin
steps: Simmer the pork with half the onion, 2 garlic cloves, bay leaf and salt in 2 litres water for 1.5 hours until tender; shred and keep 500 ml broth.
Toast and soak the chiles, then blend with the remaining garlic and onion, oregano, cumin and a cup of broth and strain.
Fry the chile sauce in the lard in a wide pot for 5 minutes over medium heat, then add the hominy and shredded pork.
Cook, stirring, for 15-20 minutes, adding broth little by little until the hominy absorbs it and the dish is moist but not soupy.
Serve dry-style on plates with shredded cabbage, radish, onion, lime and tostadas.

ingredients: 1.5 kg pork leg or shoulder plus 500 g pork ribs, in large chunks
250 ml coconut vinegar (vinagre de tuba; substitute apple cider vinegar)
6 guajillo chiles and 3 ancho chiles, seeded
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp black peppercorns, 4 cloves, 2 bay leaves
steps: Toast the chiles, soak them in the coconut vinegar for 20 minutes, then blend with ginger, garlic, coriander, cumin, pepper, cloves and salt into a thick adobo.
Coat the pork thoroughly and marinate overnight in the fridge.

ingredients: 2 g instant yeast (optional, for a more reliable rise)
steps: Mix the flour, starter, water, sugar and yeast, rest 30 minutes, then add the salt and knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Let rise 3-4 hours at room temperature with two folds, then refrigerate overnight to develop the characteristic sour, salty flavour.
Divide into 8 pieces, shape into torpedoes about 18 cm long with tapered ends, and proof 1.5 hours until puffy.
Slash each roll once lengthwise and bake at 230 C with steam (a tray of boiling water) for 20-25 minutes until deep golden and the crust crackles.
Cool on a rack; the thick crust is what lets the birote hold up when drowned for tortas ahogadas.

ingredients: 150 g piloncillo, grated, or dark brown sugar
120 ml vegetable oil or melted butter
1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp baking powder
steps: Heat the oven to 175 C and grease a 23 x 13 cm loaf pan.
Whisk the mashed bananas with the eggs, oil and piloncillo until smooth.
Fold in the flour, soda, powder, canela and salt until just combined, then add the nuts.
Bake 55-60 minutes until a skewer in the centre comes out clean and the top is dark golden.

ingredients: 1 vanilla bean, split (or 2 tsp vanilla extract)
steps: Heat the milk with the cinnamon, vanilla and sugar until steaming, then steep off the heat for 15 minutes and cool slightly.
Whisk the yolks and egg with the salt, slowly whisk in the warm milk, and strain into 6 heatproof ramekins.
Bake in a water bath at 160 C for 30-35 minutes until just set with a slight wobble in the centre.
Slide under a hot grill for 2-4 minutes until the tops develop dark, burnished spots, the signature of Guadalajara jericalla.
Chill at least 2 hours and serve cold.

ingredients: 1 papaya, 1 cantaloupe slice, 2 bananas, 2 apples, 1 cup strawberries, all diced
1/2 cup Mexican crema or sour cream

Top with granola, coconut and raisins and serve immediately, as sold on Guadalajara street carts.

ingredients: ice and coarse rock salt, for churning

Pour into a metal can (garrafa) set in a wooden tub packed with ice and rock salt, and spin the can by hand, scraping the frozen mixture from the sides with a paddle, for 20-30 minutes until thick (or use an ice-cream machine).
Serve immediately in cups; in Jalisco common flavours include vanilla, lime, mamey and tuna (prickly pear).

ingredients: 500 g fresh corn masa (or masa harina mixed with water)
lime sorbet (nieve de limón) and chile powder, to serve

Serve very cold over ice with lime juice and salt, a scoop of lime sorbet and a sprinkle of chile powder.

ingredients: pinch salt, chile powder for the rim, ice

60 ml pomegranate juice or 2 tbsp grenadine

steps: Stir the orange, pomegranate and lime juices together with the chile, salt and onion.

Serve ice-cold in small caballito glasses as a sweet-sour-spicy chaser beside tequila.

ingredients: 1 litre fresh tuba (coconut palm sap), bought same-day from a licensed vendor (substitute fresh coconut water)

1 white onion, half sliced, half for grilling
2 tsp coarse salt and 1 tsp black pepper
2 tbsp beef tallow or vegetable oil
12 green onions (cebollitas) and 6 jalapeños, for grilling

1 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp dried oregano
steps: Trim the membrane from the skirt and pound lightly to an even thickness.
Mix the juices, beer, soy, Worcestershire, garlic, onion, pepper, oregano and oil, and marinate the meat 4 hours in the fridge.
Pat dry, salt just before cooking and grill over very hot charcoal 3-4 minutes per side until well charred and medium.

ingredients: 1.5 kg beef chuck short ribs (agujas), cut thin across the bone
steps: Light a mesquite or hardwood charcoal fire and let it burn to steady medium-hot coals.

Grill 5-6 minutes per side until the fat is rendered and crisp and the meat is cooked through, moving pieces off the hottest spot if flare-ups occur.

ingredients: 1 young milk-fed kid goat (cabrito, about 5-6 kg), split, or 2.5 kg kid legs and ribs
steps: Rub the cabrito all over with mashed garlic, lard and coarse salt.
Spread it open on a steel cross (estaca) or long skewers and plant it at an angle about 60 cm from a bed of glowing mesquite embers, Monterrey style.
Roast slowly for 2.5-3 hours, turning every 30 minutes, until the skin is golden and crisp and the meat pulls cleanly off the bone with clear juices.

steps: Heat a plough disc (disco) or large wok over a wood or gas fire and fry the bacon 8 minutes until crisp.

ingredients: 1 kg beef sirloin or chuck, in 2 cm cubes
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp pepper

Serve with arroz rojo, refried beans and flour tortillas.

ingredients: 1.2 kg pork shoulder, in 3 cm cubes
8 chiles colorados (dried Anaheim or New Mexico chiles), seeded
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp dried oregano, 2 bay leaves
steps: Simmer the pork in salted water just to cover for 30 minutes, then drain and keep the broth.
Soak the chiles in hot water 15 minutes and blend with garlic, cumin, oregano, orange juice and 500 ml broth; strain.
Fry the pork in lard over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes until browned.

10 dried chiles de la tierra (New Mexico or Anaheim chiles), seeded
1 tsp cumin and 1 tsp dried oregano
steps: Toast and soak the chiles 15 minutes, then blend with garlic, onion, cumin, oregano and 500 ml water; strain.
Season the beef with salt and brown it in lard over high heat in batches, then sprinkle with flour and stir 2 minutes.

ingredients: 8 ancho chiles, seeded (or a mix of ancho and guajillo)
1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp black pepper
steps: Simmer the pork with salt in water to cover for 1.5 hours until tender; let the water nearly evaporate, then shred the meat finely.

Fry the shredded pork in the lard in a wide pan over medium heat for 10 minutes until lightly crisp.

vegetable oil for frying, about 500 ml

ingredients: 1 kg pork shoulder, sliced 5 mm thick
120 ml pineapple juice and 3 tbsp white vinegar
3 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp oregano, 1.5 tsp salt
chopped onion, cilantro, lime and salsa verde to serve

ingredients: 400 g raw shrimp, peeled and chopped
200 g asadero or Monterey Jack, grated
1 poblano chile, roasted, peeled and chopped
steps: Melt the butter over medium heat and cook the onion and poblano 4 minutes.

steps: Spread refried beans on 4 tortillas and top each with meat and cheese.

ingredients: 1 litre goat's milk (or half cow's milk)

ingredients: 1 whole red snapper (1.2 kg) or 4 fillets, cleaned
4 chiles güeros en escabeche (pickled yellow chiles)
2 bay leaves, 1/2 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
steps: Score the fish, rub with lime juice and salt, and leave for 10 minutes.
Heat the olive oil over medium heat and fry the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft; add tomatoes, bay, oregano and cinnamon and simmer 10 minutes into a chunky sauce.
Stir in olives, capers and chiles, then nestle the fish into the sauce and spoon sauce over it.

ingredients: 4 tomatoes, blended with 1/2 onion and 3 garlic cloves
2 sprigs epazote and a handful of parsley, chopped
steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the rice over medium heat for 5 minutes until lightly golden.

Add the crabs, squid, jalapeño and epazote and simmer 10 minutes.

ingredients: 6 blue crabs (jaiba), cleaned, or 400 g crab meat plus 1 litre seafood stock
3 chiles anchos or 2 chipotles in adobo
2 tbsp masa harina, dissolved in 100 ml water
steps: Boil the crabs in the water for 15 minutes; remove, pick some meat and return the shells to the pot to make a stock, then strain.
Toast and soak the anchos, then blend with the charred tomatoes, onion and garlic.
Fry the purée in oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, add the crab stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the masa slurry and epazote and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened; add the crab meat and claws and heat through.
Serve hot with lime and tortillas; a Veracruz hangover cure.

ingredients: 12 very fresh oysters, shucked (from a trusted supplier), or extra shrimp
250 ml tomato ketchup and 200 ml tomato-clam juice or tomato juice

Bake at 220 °C with a tray of hot water in the oven for 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.

ingredients: 100 g vegetable shortening, 100 g icing sugar and 100 g flour for the topping
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the eggs, milk and vanilla, knead 8 minutes, then knead in the butter until the dough is soft and glossy.
Cover and let rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Make the topping by rubbing the shortening, icing sugar and flour into a paste; flavour half with cocoa.
Divide the dough into 12 balls on lined trays, press a thin disc of topping onto each and score it in a shell pattern with a knife or concha cutter.
Rise 1 hour, then bake at 180 °C for 18–20 minutes until the bread is lightly golden underneath.

ingredients: 120 g sugar, plus 100 g for coating
120 g butter, softened, plus 50 g melted
1 tbsp orange blossom water (agua de azahar)
steps: Combine the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the eggs, milk, orange blossom water and zest and knead 8 minutes, then knead in the softened butter until smooth and elastic.
Cover and rise 1.5–2 hours until doubled.
Reserve a quarter of the dough; shape the rest into 2 round loaves, and from the reserve roll thin "bone" ropes with knobs and small balls; lay bones across each loaf and a ball on top.
Rise 45 minutes, brush with beaten yolk and bake at 180 °C for 30–35 minutes until deep golden.
Brush the warm bread with melted butter and dust heavily with sugar; serve for Día de Muertos with hot chocolate.

ingredients: 1 tbsp orange zest and 1 tbsp orange blossom water
150 g candied fruit strips (ate, figs, candied orange)
100 g shortening, 100 g icing sugar and 100 g flour for the sugar paste
1 small oven-safe figurine (niño) wrapped in foil, optional
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the eggs, milk, zest and orange blossom water and knead 10 minutes, then work in the butter until silky; rise 2 hours.
Shape the dough into a long rope and join it into a large oval ring on a lined tray; push the figurine in from underneath if using.
Rub the shortening, icing sugar and flour into a paste, roll into strips and lay them across the ring alternating with candied fruit.
Rise 45 minutes, brush with beaten egg and bake at 180 °C for 30–35 minutes until golden.
Cool and slice on 6 January with hot chocolate; whoever finds the figurine hosts tamales on 2 February.

ingredients: 120 g cream cheese, softened (optional, for flan napolitano)
steps: Melt the sugar in a pan over medium heat without stirring, swirling until it becomes an amber caramel, then pour it into a 22 cm round mould and tilt to coat the base.
Blend the eggs, condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream cheese and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the custard over the set caramel, cover with foil and set the mould in a larger pan of hot water (baño María).
Bake at 175 °C for 55–60 minutes until the edges are set and the centre wobbles slightly.
Cool, chill at least 4 hours, then run a knife round the edge and invert onto a plate so the caramel flows over.

500 ml whipping cream and 3 tbsp icing sugar for topping

Bake in a greased 23 x 33 cm pan at 175 °C for 25–30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk and milk; poke holes all over the warm cake and pour the milks over slowly until absorbed.

250 g piloncillo (unrefined cone sugar), chopped (sub dark brown sugar)
150 g queso añejo or Monterey Jack, grated
